interface_sections.Statement:
Assume the flat effective LAD postulate [[post-rpm-lad-effective-equation]] with $\tau_e>0$ and take $F\equiv0$. In Minkowski coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, choose constants $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, $A\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ with units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$. Define for all $\tau\in\mathbb R$

$$\theta(\tau):=\theta_0+A\tau_e e^{(\tau-\tau_0)/\tau_e},\qquad U(\tau):=c(\cosh\theta(\tau),\sinh\theta(\tau),0,0),$$

and let $x(\tau)=x_0+\int_{\tau_0}^{\tau}U(s)\,ds$. Then $x$ is a smooth future-timelike worldline parametrized by proper time, and it solves the adopted LAD equation with zero external force. Its proper acceleration magnitude is

$$\sqrt{\eta(a,a)}=c|A|e^{(\tau-\tau_0)/\tau_e},$$

so it grows exponentially as $\tau\to+\infty$. By contrast, the force-free reduced LL field in [[lem-rpm-ll-reduced-ode]] is zero on the shell and has constant-velocity solutions. This is a counterexample about the adopted ODEs, not an observed phenomenon or a statement about finite-body electrodynamics.

interface_sections.Definition:
Use the charged/spinning body-model conventions of the now-authored batch-24 carrier [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ in metres, $c>0$, and a $C^2$ future timelike representative curve $z:I\to M$ parametrized by proper time $\tau$ in seconds, with $U=dz/d\tau$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The actual supplier defines these quantities and the SI electromagnetic-tensor convention used here. Assume Countable Choice for the GR smooth-structure, convex-normal and parallel-transport suppliers used below.

**(a) Flat isolated-body moments.** In an inertial chart of affine Minkowski space, let $T^{ab}$ be a smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor with components in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and spatially compact support on every finite time slab. At a fixed time $t$, define
$$p^a(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}T^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\,d^3x,$$
and, for a representative point $z(t)$ on that time slice, define
$$S_z^{ab}(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}\left((x-z(t))^aT^{0b}(ct,\mathbf x)-(x-z(t))^bT^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\right)d^3x.$$
Here $(x-z(t))^0=0$ on the chosen slice, $p$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $S_z$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$. These are definitions of moments; no conservation is asserted by clause (a).

**(b) Local curved-body moments.** Let $z\in M$ and let $U_0$ be a convex normal neighborhood containing $z$. Let $\Sigma\subset U_0$ be a spacelike $C^1$ hypersurface through $z$, with future unit normal $n_x$ and induced volume element $d\Sigma$. Let a smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor $T^{ab}$ have support on $\Sigma$ compactly contained in $U_0$, with all displayed integrals finite. For each support point $x\in\Sigma$, let $v(x):=\exp_z^{-1}(x)\in T_zM$ be the unique joining position vector supplied by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]] and [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $H_{x\to z}:T_xM\to T_zM$ be parallel transport along that unique geodesic, with existence, uniqueness and metric preservation as in [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]. Define $T^\sharp(n_x)^a:=T^{ab}(x)(n_x)_b$ and
$$p_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,\qquad S_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma v(x)\wedge H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,$$
where $(v\wedge w)^{ab}:=v^aw^b-v^bw^a$ and the finite-dimensional vector and tensor integrals are taken componentwise in any basis of $T_zM$. The resulting $p_z$ and $S_z$ are a vector and an antisymmetric tensor at $z$; their units are $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$.

Fix $m>0$ kilograms, $q\in\mathbb R$ coulombs and $c>0$ metres per second. For a chosen constant $b\in\mathbb R$ in tesla, put

$$\chi(x)=\frac b2(x^1)^2,\qquad A=d\chi=b x^1\,dx^1.$$

Here $\chi$ has units tesla metre squared and the covector components $A_a$ have units tesla metres. Then $F=dA=0$. On every finite $C^2$ future-timelike segment $z:[\tau_0,\tau_1]\to\mathcal A$ with $\tau_0<\tau_1$, proper-time parameter in seconds and fixed endpoint events $X_0,X_1$, the action differs from its zero-potential value by

$$S_A[z]-S_0[z]=q\bigl(\chi(X_1)-\chi(X_0)\bigr).$$

Thus its stationary curves are precisely the free massive straight timelike curves on these segments. Their kinetic momentum $P=mU$, $U=dz/d\tau$, is constant. With $p=mU^\flat$ and the local canonical covector $\pi_A=p+qA$ of [[lem-rpm-charge-gauge-boundary]],

$$\pi_{A,1}=mU_1+qb x^1,\qquad \frac{d\pi_{A,1}}{d\tau}=qb U^1.$$

The raised and lowered spatial components agree in this chart. This canonical component can vary when $qbU^1\ne0$, while the Lorentz force and kinetic-momentum derivative vanish. If any factor vanishes, the canonical component is constant too. The shift is a gauge-dependent covector calculation, not a force or an energy measurement.

interface_sections.Remark:
The present pair prescribes an external field and adopts the flat LAD equation as a separate effective model. It does not construct a coupled Maxwell field sourced by a point charge or evaluate a self-field on the worldline. [[def-rpm-body-moments]] defines moments for a smooth finite body (and a local curved moment convention); its definitions do not assert a point limit or a self-force law.

The point-charge field is singular on the worldline, as reviewed by Poisson, Pound, and Vega; a self-force treatment therefore requires a specified regularization or extended-body limiting argument. Gralla, Harte, and Wald prove results for a particular one-parameter family of exact flat Maxwell–matter solutions in which body size, charge, and mass scale toward zero while the charge-to-mass ratio has a limit. Their leading motion is Lorentz-force motion and their first-order description includes self-force and multipole corrections. Their separate reduced-order discussion is qualified to regimes with negligible dipole and spin contributions.
